extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants and prosecution practitioners (patent attorneys/agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on filing after-final responses and options for progressing prosecution after a final rejection in U.S. patent applications, including the (now-closed) AFCP 2.0 eligibility and practical alternatives such as RCEs, pre-appeal, interviews, and appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program goal — reduce RCEs and improve collaboration
rubrics_metrics.description: The goal of AFCP 2.0 was to improve pendency by reducing the number of Requests for Continued Examination (RCE) and encourage increased collaboration between applicant and examiner to advance prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use after-final amendment programs (when available) to resolve outstanding issues without filing an RCE; engage with examiner to attempt to advance prosecution rather than immediately pursuing RCE or appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: No additional program fees required
rubrics_metrics.description: No additional fees required (only standard fees like extensions of time).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When deciding whether to use a program like AFCP 2.0, account only for standard statutory/processing fees; applicants need not plan for special program charges (AFCP 2.0 had no extra fee). Note: program has been terminated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner time allocation for after-final amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner could spend up to 3 hours considering after-final amendments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare focused, high-value amendments and arguments that can be evaluated within a limited examiner time budget; prioritize amendments likely to place application in condition for allowance or materially improve position for appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviews allowed and expected collaboration
rubrics_metrics.description: AFCP 2.0 could include interview between examiner and applicant and applicants must be willing to participate in interview if necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to request and participate in an interview to explain amendments/arguments; use interviews to clarify issues and narrow dispute efficiently rather than exchanging lengthy paper arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited claim amendments allowed after final rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Allowed limited claim amendments after final rejection (subject to AFCP 2.0 requirements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments after final should be narrowly tailored (not broadening) and aimed at overcoming specific rejections or improving form for appeal; avoid broad changes that would be inappropriate in an after-final context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement — file a response under 37 CFR 1.116
rubrics_metrics.description: To qualify for AFCP 2.0: File a response under 37 CFR 1.116.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the after-final response is filed under the correct regulatory provision (37 CFR 1.116) to be eligible for program consideration; follow all procedural requirements of that rule when preparing the response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement — amendment to at least one independent claim (no broadening)
rubrics_metrics.description: To qualify for AFCP 2.0: Include an amendment to at least one independent claim that does NOT broaden scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any independent-claim amendment must be narrowing (or at least not broaden). Draft claim changes to clearly reduce scope or correct formal/clarifying language rather than expand claim scope; explicitly note narrowing effect in remarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement — submit Form PTO/SB/434
rubrics_metrics.description: To qualify for AFCP 2.0: Submit Form PTO/SB/434 (request for AFCP 2.0 consideration).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete and include the required program request form with the after-final response so the examiner and docketing staff can identify the submission as an AFCP 2.0 request; ensure form information matches the response and amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program termination and cost considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: For fiscal year 2022, the USPTO estimates it expended more than $15 million in costs associated with examiners considering AFCP 2.0 submissions; program ended partly due to public concerns about proposed fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating procedural options, weigh PTO resource considerations and potential future program availability; if a program would require new fees, consider whether the benefits justify cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard after-final practice — goal of amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed amendments should place the application either in condition for allowance or in better form for appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft after-final amendments with the narrow objective of securing allowance or improving the appellate record (e.g., clarifying claim scope, addressing examiner's key grounds). Avoid extensive rewriting that cannot be justified after final rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard after-final practice — limited scope of allowable amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Limited scope of allowable amendments in standard after-final practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize the constraints on what can be changed after a final action; focus on pinpointed amendments that respond directly to examiner rejections and avoid introducing new matter or broadening.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner interviews as a post-final tool
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-appeal request interviews available; examiner interviews cannot extend the time period but are beneficial for clarifying issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use interviews to identify whether the rejection is amenable to amendment or argument and to narrow issues before committing to RCE or appeal; schedule interviews early and prepare a concise agenda and supporting record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-Appeal Brief Conference Request — concise argument format
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-Appeal Brief Conference Request: 5-page summary of arguments reviewed by a panel of examiners; cheaper alternative to full appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare a tight 5-page presentation that prioritizes the strongest errors in the examiner's rejections; use the conference to seek identification of clear errors that can be corrected without full appeal expense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for Continued Examination (RCE) — when to choose
rubrics_metrics.description: RCE reopens prosecution, requires a higher fee, and allows broader amendments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose an RCE when broader amendments or further examination are necessary to resolve outstanding issues; weigh the fee and pendency cost against the need for substantive changes or further prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Appeal + Appeal Brief (PTAB) — tradeoffs
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice of Appeal and Appeal Brief leads to PTAB review; is the most expensive option and provides the most rigorous review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider appeal when the disagreement is primarily legal or where a robust adversarial review is needed; anticipate higher cost and longer timeline but potentially binding PTAB precedent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic consideration — plan after-final response at time of final office action
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider after-final response strategy at time of final office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When drafting responses to a final office action, anticipate downstream choices (after-final amendments, pre-appeal, RCE, appeal) and tailor the record and amendments to preserve options and strengthen later arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-AFCP strategic posture — reliance on RCEs and appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may rely more on RCEs and appeals after AFCP 2.0 closure; pre-appeal conferences and interviews gain importance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust prosecution strategy to increased use of RCEs and appeals where necessary, while maximizing use of low-cost options (pre-appeal, interviews) to resolve issues before committing to higher-cost measures.
